title: Does Concealing Gender Identity Help Women Win the Competition? An Empirical Investigation into Online Video Games
authors: Xinlei Chen; Xiaohua Zeng; Cheng Zhang
eligible_reason: Not a DiD. Player-pair PVP fight-level panel: player fixed-effects regressions (xtreg, fe) of the logit win rate on the opponent's virtual (in-game) gender and gender-combination dummies with level, experience, PVP-count and role-interaction controls, plus a propensity-score-matched comparison of players choosing female vs male avatars. No treatment switching on at unit-specific dates.
design_notes: Code.TXT: SAS data steps build logit_win from tot_win/tot_lose per fight and a logit propensity score (logit_p) for choosing a female virtual gender, then 1:1 matching (treat/control datasets). Stata: xtset characterid; xtreg logit_win op_v_gender (or op_male op_female; mf_j fm_j ff_j) op_currentcharacterlevel currentcharacterlevel ratio_experience ratio_pvp role11-role44, fe vce(robust) (Code.TXT lines 154-167). Cross-sectional comparison across opponents, not a policy adoption.
data_files: Replication files/Replication files/Dataset.csv (159,914 player-pair fight rows)
data_files_note: Readme.txt: 'Dataset.csv is the disguised data. Noises/multipliers have been added to the variables.'
data_provenance_note: Noise and multipliers added to the variables (Readme.txt).
software_notes: SAS 9.4 for data processing, Stata 15.1 for regressions (Code.TXT).
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available locally (data/text/mksc and papers/mksc checked Nov 2); the OpenAlex abstract in data/frame/mksc.jsonl is a one-sentence summary. Design read from the README and the main-results code; no package code was run.
